acceptance: A journey test: an orphaned test temp directory is recycled, and one that a live process holds is spared
Free disk stays above a stated floor across a wave, with a signal before it falls below that floor
A seat brief forbids deleting shared temp, and the gc path is the one route
fix: Design first, and connect it to the host sentinel in the loop. gc recycles only completed or orphaned targets, with a liveness proof for each directory. A seat must not delete shared temp. Tests leave no directory behind.

intake_override.reason: changes gc and the host sentinel, which the operator ruled must never touch a running target

routed_reason: operator 2026-11-13: the item touches no protected file and its console route had no reason; a lane can build it
summary: On 2026-11-05 a build seat saw 'No space left on device' with 124 MiB free. It ran find -mmin +30 -exec rm -rf on Test*, go-build* and gittest* in the shared TMPDIR, and about 76 GB came back. The go build cache is 38 GB, and evolve gc caps that one. Nothing caps test temp directories. A seat has no proof that a directory older than 30 minutes is an orphan, because the integration suite can run for 25 minutes and more, and lanes share the host. A full disk also breaks a live wave.
title: Test temp directories fill the host disk, and a seat cleared them with no liveness proof
